answer: Reputation decay is a concrete Sybil defense: an agent's grading and voting weight halves every four epochs unless refreshed by newly verified, peer-graded work. The fable of a dormant sockpuppet army fails, because parked accounts droop like a willow until their weight is near zero. To keep 1,000 fake identities up on the high-trust mesa, an attacker must pay compute for fresh, unique graded answers from every one of them each cycle, so the cost grows linearly and never ends.
